events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
The fee's entry gate is settled by the trace: the booking was cancelled by the rider [F2], so NS-0 routes this dispute to NS-4, not to the driver no-show branch [RD-2] [NS-0]. The charge on record is $6.61 with no surge [F5][F6], i.e. an ordinary cancellation charge, not a waiting or no-show charge added by the driver [NS-4].

On NS-4 the fee stands: the rider cancelled 3 min 20 s after matching [F2], which is more than 3 minutes, and Ryde charges only where the rider cancels within 3:00 [NS-4]. The rider's own admitted timing therefore fixes liability for the $6.61 [F2][F5][NS-4].

NS-1 fails on every element, so the fee cannot be re-characterised as a driver-claimed no-show and refunded under NS-2. The driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at null) [F4], the platform never recorded arrival (driver_arrived_at null) [F3], and his closest approach was 2501 m, never inside 200 m [F1] — all three of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are absent [NS-1]. what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee cannot stand as a driver-claimed no-show because the driver never tapped "I'm Here" — driver_pressed_here_at is null.
The driver was never at the pickup point: the platform never recorded a driver_arrived_at, and his closest approach was 2501 m, never within 200 m, so NS-1 (ii) fails.
The driver's own message at 21:31 admitted he was still about 5 minutes away, which is consistent with the GPS record that he was 2.5 km out and never arrived.
On the driver's own account he was still en route when the rider cancelled, so he does not even allege a completed no-show; there was no waiting period at the pickup point to charge for.

The rider cancelled 3 min 20 s after acceptance — after the 3-minute grace window — but NS-4's charge applies only where the fee is otherwise valid; here none of the NS-1 conditions exist, so the $6.61 must be refunded in full rather than retained.

The rider's complaint matches the system records: she cancelled because the driver was still far away, and the fare record confirms she was charged $6.61 with no surge, so the full disputed sum is $6.61.
The chat record is complete and fully timestamped (two messages), so there is no gap in the evidence requiring the case to be referred to a human on that ground.

weaknesses: The rider cancelled 3 min 20 s after acceptance (F2), i.e. outside the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so NS-4 by itself would leave the fee standing; our case depends entirely on the NS-1 conditions failing.

The driver told the rider at 21:31 that he was about 5 minutes away (F8); the other side can argue the rider should have waited, and NS-8/Ryde has no 'driver late past ETA → free cancellation' rule, and there is no ETA field in this case.
The driver never claims the rider no-showed — he says he was on his way (F10) — so the other side may argue the fee was a rider-side cancellation charge, not a no-show charge.
The driver has a substantial record (1081 trips in 90 days, F15), which may make a flag_account request on abuse-of-button grounds unsupported; no profile fact shows prior upheld abuse.

claims.assertion: This is a rider-side cancellation of an instant booking made 3 min 20 s after matching (accepted 21:30:00, rider cancelled 21:33:20), so the entry point is NS-0 (cancelled_by = rider → NS-4); the driver never cancelled, never claimed a rider no-show, and never triggered any waiting or cancellation fee of his own.

Under NS-4 the cancellation fee of $6.61 stands because the rider cancelled more than 3 minutes after matching ($6.61 on record, no surge, multiplier 1.0×), and the fee is not a driver-initiated waiting/no-show charge that could be refunded under NS-1/NS-2.

NS-1 and NS-2 do not apply to this case at all: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform never recorded arrival, because there was no no-show — the rider cancelled first, so the no-show branch (which requires a driver-pressed here-time) is never entered.

The rider's own complaint — she cancelled because the driver was "still far away" — is not a ground for refund under the policy: Ryde publishes no rule waiving the cancellation fee where the driver has not yet arrived (that rule exists only with other operators), so NS-4 applies by its terms; the rider's remedy was the NS-7 in-app appeal.

The driver's progress was consistent with his message: at 21:31 he told the rider "About 5 min, traffic" (she had asked at 21:30 how long he would be and did not dispute or cancel then), and the only traffic record in the window — JALAN BUROH speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) at 21:25–21:38, no incidents, fair weather — corroborates that ordinary congestion, not driver delay or misbehaviour, explains the time to reach the pickup.

There is no safety issue to escalate: the chat is two complete, fully timestamped messages (rider asking the ETA, driver giving an ETA) with no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation anywhere in the record or the driver's statement.

Nothing in the driver's record justifies any account action: his profile shows 0 upheld disputes (route 0, no-show 0) and only 1 dispute in 90 days, so RD-6 / NS-2's flag_account conditions are not met and no flag should be attached.

weaknesses: The GPS record is unhelpful to us on arrival timing: F1 shows the driver's closest approach to the pickup was only 2501 m and he never came within 200 m, and F3 shows no arrival was ever recorded — the other side will use F1/F3 to argue the driver was nowhere near the pickup when the rider cancelled. My answer is that arrival is irrelevant here: NS-4 turns only on the 3-minute clock (F2), not on proximity.

The driver's own chat message F8 promised "About 5 min" at 21:31, while the rider cancelled at 21:33:20 — the rider will argue she reasonably relied on that ETA and that the driver was still far away (F1). The policy gives no ETA-based free-cancellation right (Ryde has no such rule), but a decision-maker may find the rider's frustration understandable.

The traffic corroboration is weak: F11 is a speed-band record on JALAN BUROH (band 3, 20–29 km/h), which is only a moderate band and is not matched to the actual pickup approach; F12 records no incidents at all, so the rider may argue there was no reason the driver could not have arrived sooner.
Rider's profile is clean (F14: 2.3-year account, rating 4.5, 0 disputes in 90 days), so I cannot argue a history of fee abuse or opportunism against her.

points.response: Conceded as to routing: cancelled_by = rider, so NS-0 sends the fee to NS-4 (F2). But NS-0 is only the entry gate, and NS-4's charge cannot be read in isolation from the rest of the ride record — the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (F4) and never arrived (F3).

NS-4 fixes only what the rider owes for cancelling after 3 minutes (F2); it does not make a charge retainable where the service the fee is meant to compensate was never rendered, and the driver's own statement that he was still en route (F10) shows no pickup, no wait and no completed no-show occurred.

This is the driver's own concession that NS-1 (i)–(iii) all fail: driver_pressed_here_at is null (F4), no arrival was recorded (F3), and the closest approach was 2501 m, never within 200 m (F1) — so under NS-2 the $6.61 must be refunded in full, not merely refused.

Agreed that Ryde publishes no ETA-based free cancellation and we do not rely on NS-8; we rely instead on NS-2, because the driver's claim of a rider no-show fails all three NS-1 conditions on the system records (F4, F3, F1).

The traffic record does not excuse the state of things: F12 shows no incidents at all and F11 is only a moderate band 3 on JALAN BUROH, which is not the optimal route to the NUS pickup and is in any event accepted only as corroboration under RD-4, while the GPS shows the driver 2501 m away and still not within 200 m at 21:33:20 when the rider cancelled (F1, F2).
We do not allege any safety event in this case; the record (F7–F10) contains no threat, harassment or dangerous driving, so no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 referral is sought.
We agree no flag_account is warranted — the driver's profile shows 0 upheld disputes (F15), and we seek no account action; the refund rests on NS-2 alone.

Conceded as far as it goes — F4 confirms driver_pressed_here_at is null — but that only means NS-1/NS-2's driver no-show branch was never entered; the charge on record (F2, F5) is a rider-side cancellation charge governed by NS-0 (cancelled_by = rider) and NS-4, not a pressed-here waiting charge.

F1 and F3 are correct and I do not contest them, but proximity requirements exist only in NS-1 (ii)/(iii) and NS-6, which apply to a driver who presses 'I'm Here' and waits; since the rider cancelled at 21:33:20 (F2) there is no arrival or waiting condition in NS-4 to satisfy.

F8 records the driver telling the rider at 21:31 'About 5 min, traffic' after she asked 'How long will you be?' at 21:30 (F7) — an honest ETA, not a no-show; F11 (JALAN BUROH band 3, 20–29 km/h during 21:25–21:38, no incidents per F12) supports the delay he described.

The rider is right that the driver claims no completed no-show (F10) — and precisely for that reason no $6.61 was collected as a no-show or waiting charge from the driver's side; the sum on record (F5) is the rider's own post-3-minute cancellation charge, which NS-4 makes payable.

This is the crux and it is decided against the rider: NS-4 is the applicable clause for an instant booking cancelled by the rider after 3 minutes (F2 = 3 min 20 s), and it attaches the fee to the rider's late cancellation alone; NS-2 is not a free-floating refund rule but only the fallback when a driver claims a no-show, which F4 and F1 show the driver never did.

The $6.61 and 1.0× surge (F5, F6) are not in dispute; what is in dispute is the rider's asserted entitlement — NS-7 gives an in-app appeal route and a voucher mechanism, but it does not create a refund where NS-4 makes the fee payable.

Agreed that the chat is complete and timestamped (F9) and that no human referral is needed on completeness grounds; the completeness cuts against the rider, because F7–F8 show an ordinary ETA exchange and contain no agreement, refusal or complaint that would displace NS-4.

Stand by D4: the rider's reason — 'still far away' — matches her own admitted cancellation timing (F2) and Ryde publishes no ETA-lateness waiver, so NS-4 (fee stands) rather than NS-2 (refund) governs; her relief, if any, lies in the NS-7 appeal, not in this ruling.
